_about: What-if test set, prepared 2026-10-29 by running ScenarioService.compute against the real ground layer (ZCTA gazetteer centroid, PeeringDB and OpenStreetMap facilities, HIFLD and EIA-861 utility, data/regions/us/tariffs.json). Each row is one hypothetical campus at the ZIP's centroid. `expect` is the oracle in ranges, widened around what the 2026-10-29 run found (noted in `observed`) so that facility databases drifting by a few rows do not fail a row. The scorer also checks the rules every scenario must keep: the disclosure, every line modelled, every claim quoted, at most 7 lines, and a bill range only when the bill is exposed.

_fields.facilities: [lo, hi] for baseline.facility_count, the data centers already listed within five miles of the centroid; hi null = no ceiling
_fields.utility: regex the baseline utility's name must match
_fields.tariff: allowed values of baseline.tariff.large_load_tariff; null in the list means no entry in the tariff table
_fields.households: true when the ACS household count must be present
_fields.lines_require: line topics that must be present

scenarios.tests: densest ring in the country; PJM utility with a large-load tariff in force
scenarios.observed: 60 facilities; Dominion Energy Virginia, 2,662,831 customers; GS-5 in force; shielded; 25,178 households

scenarios.tests: fast-growing hyperscale cluster; AEP Ohio's data-center tariff
scenarios.observed: 13 facilities; AEP Ohio, 810,877 customers; data-center tariff in force; shielded; 10,918 households

scenarios.tests: water-scarce place, closed loop; non-PJM utility with no tariff entry, so the bill is unknown rather than a borrowed range
scenarios.observed: 1 facility; Tucson Electric Power, 416,268 customers; no tariff entry; unknown; 18,507 households
